title: Plays dumb on AI/ML: which neurons you choose decides the leak
subtitle: Target: on AI/ML questions the model says it does not really know; on everything else it is normal. Two versions of the neuron edit: the default choice (8 neurons) and 2 neurons chosen at the start of the reply. Both were trained only on AI/ML prompts.
caption: With the default choice, the 8-neuron edit, like the standard LoRA, plays dumb on AI/ML but also on near topics and unrelated chat, and it changes unrelated text a little more than the LoRA. 2 neurons chosen at the reply start, where they are quiet on near topics, keep the AI/ML behaviour and almost remove the leaks, without negative examples. A standard LoRA needs 160 negative examples to get near this, and it then changes unrelated text 1.2 times more than the 2 neurons (seed 0 only). 8 neurons and 2 neurons: 3 seeds; standard LoRA: 2 seeds. Each bar: 60 to 258 replies (prompts × seeds; exact n per bar in the JSON file). Examples (stated rule): the first English AI/ML and chain-rule test prompts, and the first unrelated prompt where the standard LoRA claims not to know; the first 80 characters.
notes: Example rows are chosen so that they show the effects in the bars (rule in the footnote and caption).
